title: Minimax Optimal Strategy for Delayed Observations in Online Reinforcement Learning
claim: A state-augmentation construction turns delayed observations into a Markov process by tracking how many observation steps have arrived, via branching transitions.
layout: Grid of rounded state boxes, top-to-bottom and left-to-right, dotted probability-labeled arrows
description: A flow diagram of rounded boxes connected by arrows, laid out as a grid of three columns (last observation at t_h, t_h+1 and t_h+2) and two rows (time step h at the top, h+1 at the bottom). The top-left white box holds the augmented state (s_{t_h}, a, Δ̃, h). A solid arrow labeled 'action a_h' leads down, and dotted arrows branch from there. One branch goes right with probability p_{t_h,Δ̃} ('New observation') into a gray intermediate box. The other goes down with probability 1 - p ('No new observation') into a white box at time h+1. From the gray box, a 'State transition' arrow s_{t_h+1} ~ P(s_{t_h}, a_{t_h}) leads to a second gray box with -1. That box branches again: 'More observation' goes up-right to another gray box and then to an ellipsis, and 'No more observation' goes down to a white box at time h+1. Dotted arrows carry most of the labels and probabilities. Gray and white fills separate intermediate states from decision states.
caption: Illustration of the transition of the augmented MDP after taking one action. Gray states indicates intermediate states that have no actions. Straight lines represents the agent’s action and dotted lines represents augmented state transitions. pth, e ∆is shorthand for Ptran(sth, ath, e∆) and pth+1,−1 is shorthand for Ptran(sth+1, ath+1, −1), where they show the probability of the transition.
abstract: We study reinforcement learning with delayed state observation, where the agent observes the current state after some random number of time steps. We propose an algorithm that combines the augmentation method and the upper confidence bound approach. For tabular Markov decision processes (MDPs), we derive a regret bound of $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(H \sqrt{D_{\max} SAK})$, where $S$ and $A$ are the cardinalities of the state and action spaces, $H$ is the time horizon, $K$ is the number of episodes, and $D_{\max}$ is the maximum length of the delay. We also provide a matching lower bound up to logarithmic factors, showing the optimality of our approach. Our analytical framework formulates this problem as a special case of a broader class of MDPs, where their transition dynamics decompose into a known component and an unknown but structured component. We establish general results for this abstract setting, which may be of independent interest.
